elliptic: LOW — forced to ^6.6.1; mitigates transitive ECDSA risky-primitive advisory across WalletConnect/Ledger/Trezor sub-trees.

appium-uiautomator2-driver chain (HIGH: shell-quote GHSA-395f-4hp3-45gv via @appium/support + @appium/base-driver; LOW: body-parser GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6): RESOLVED 2026-08-03 — no longer an accepted residual. The evidence is the resolved tree, not a release number: a fresh npm install --package-lock-only from origin/main @ 01381d96, run in a scratch dir, resolves the nested subtree to @appium/support 7.2.6 -> shell-quote 1.10.0 and @appium/base-driver 10.7.2 -> body-parser 2.3.0, and that resolve is byte-identical to the committed lockfile, so it is main's real state and not a scratch artifact. npm audit now reports 0 critical / 0 high / 0 moderate and lists none of shell-quote, body-parser, @appium/support or @appium/base-driver as an advisory root (the remaining 18 low are the separate elliptic chain). NOTE THE SHAPE OF THE FIX — the old revisit trigger ("the nested node_modules/appium-uiautomator2-driver/node_modules/@appium/support key disappears") NEVER FIRED and was the wrong trigger: the 257-package duplicate subtree is still there, it just now duplicates PATCHED copies. Nothing was remediated deliberately; the subtree was re-resolved as a side effect of routine lockfile regeneration on 2026-07-29 — it flipped to 1.10.0 at 87e9897b (npm-minor-patch group, #1465, 07:49), regressed to 1.8.4 at ff78ac99 (i18n Phase 1 lockfile, 08:01), and was restored at 0295fd40 (regenerate package-lock.json to match package.json, 08:56), holding at 1.10.0 across every lockfile commit since. Route (4) of the four previously-failed remediations — delete the nested entries and re-resolve, npm re-derives them byte-identically at the old versions — no longer holds, because the nested ranges (appium-adb ^7.2.2, appium-android-driver ^7.2.5, teen_process ^1.8.1, express ^2.2.1) now resolve to the patched versions. The 2026-07-27 lesson stands and is exactly why this retirement is written around a lockfile diff rather than an upstream release: a version number is not evidence, npm fixAvailable is not evidence, only the resolved tree is. That entry was retired once on a version-number trigger and had to be reinstated the same day; if you are reading this while considering a similar retirement elsewhere, reproduce the resolve first. WATCHER RETIRED: veyrnox-appium-shellquote-watch deleted 2026-08-03 by the run that produced this note. Dependabot alerts #12 and #14 should resolve. NOT VERIFIED: the e2e-emulator CI job has not been re-run since the subtree moved — the Android E2E harness's entire dependency tree changed underneath it as a side effect, with no deliberate test. If that harness starts failing, look here first.

brace-expansion GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (HIGH: DoS via unbounded expansion length causing an out-of-memory process crash): ACCEPTED dev-tree residual 2026-07-26, and as of 2026-07-27 the override is TESTED AND REJECTED — do not try it again without reading this. Accounts for 29 of the 32 HIGH advisories npm audit reports on main; the other 3 are the appium/shell-quote chain noted above. The tempting fix is an overrides entry of ^5.0.8 (a patched 5.0.8 exists; the advisory range is <=5.0.7, and npm fixAvailable: false only means npm cannot reach it through existing ranges, not that no patch was published). AT THE LOCKFILE LEVEL IT LOOKS PERFECT: overrides ^5.0.8 collapses all 8 installed copies (5.0.7 x2, 2.1.2 x5, 1.1.16 x1) onto a single 5.0.8, takes npm audit from 32 HIGH to 3 HIGH, retains node_modules/appium, and leaves the 258-package appium-uiautomator2-driver subtree intact. IT BREAKS AT RUNTIME. brace-expansion 5.x changed its CommonJS export shape with no advisory-visible signal: 1.x and 2.x do module.exports = expand (a bare function), while 5.0.8 dist/commonjs exports an OBJECT { expand }. Every consumer written against the old shape throws TypeError: expand is not a function on first use. VERIFIED 2026-07-27 on a real install in a clean worktree off main: npm run lint dies immediately with that TypeError at node_modules/minimatch/minimatch.js:271 braceExpand, called from @eslint/config-array. Scope of the break: 6 of the 9 minimatch copies in the tree declare the old shape and break — root minimatch 3.1.5 (^1.1.7), 3x minimatch 5.1.9 (^2.0.1: mocha, filelist, webdriverio), 2x minimatch 9.0.9 (^2.0.2: @wdio/config, archiver-utils). Only the 3 minimatch 10.2.5 copies declare ^5.0.5 and are genuinely compatible. The root minimatch 3.1.5 is the one eslint, @eslint/eslintrc, @eslint/config-array, eslint-plugin-react, multimatch (-> javascript-obfuscator) and recursive-readdir all resolve to, so lint and the obfuscator step sit directly on the break. npm run build DOES still pass (exit 0, dist produced) — vite/rollup does not touch the broken path — so a green build is NOT evidence this override is safe. Engines are a non-issue: 5.0.8 wants node 20 || >=22 and CI runs 22 and 24. STALE BLOCKER REMOVED: the previous version of this note said evaluation was blocked because regenerating the lockfile drops appium under --legacy-peer-deps. #1372 landed, and a plain npm install --package-lock-only now retains appium and its whole subtree (verified 2026-07-27; the only removals are benign duplicate collapses like strip-ansi/string-width). That was never the real blocker — the export-shape change was, and nobody had gotten far enough to hit it. REVISIT when a brace-expansion release restores the bare-function CommonJS export, OR when the six old-shape minimatch copies are gone (i.e. eslint/mocha/wdio/archiver all move to minimatch >=10), OR if upstream backports the fix to the 1.x/2.x lines (none exists today: published lines are 1.x, 2.x, 4.x, 5.x and only 5.0.8 is patched). Risk accepted meanwhile: dev-tree only — eslint, mocha, wdio, archiver, javascript-obfuscator. Zero production impact, npm audit --omit=dev reports 0 high / 0 critical. TRACKED: watcher veyrnox-brace-expansion-watch (weekly, Mondays ~11am), added 2026-07-27. It does not watch version numbers — its decisive probe reproduces the failure directly: a scratch package.json pinning minimatch@3.1.2 with overrides brace-expansion@latest, then require('minimatch')('abd','a{b,c}d'). Still throwing TypeError: expand is not a function means unchanged; returning true means the override became viable. It also re-resolves the tree to see whether any minimatch copy still declares an old-shape ^1./^2. range, and checks for a DoS backport to the 1.x or 2.x line (which would patch the old-shape consumers without breaking them). The watcher prompt records that npm run lint is the acceptance test, NOT npm run build — the build passes even when the override is broken.
